findings.trigger: One Node stdout data callback contains two complete assistant/user/result records, or the first completed boundary followed by bytes of the next turn. Pipe coalescing makes this an ordinary supported input shape.
findings.violatedRelation: The first selected structured boundary must close the pending window. The shared classifier counts all completed boundaries, but actor_process reduces the delta to one boolean. worker_transport then adds the entire captured string before closing once. Bytes after the first boundary are included in that window.
findings.counterexample: A single captured string containing two complete recognized records increments turnBoundaryCount by two; classifyStdoutChunk returns turnBoundary:true once; observeStdoutWindow appends all bytes and emits one window. With a qualifying first segment and noise-only later segment, copying the aggregate progress flag to both future segments would also falsely renew noise.

conservedJoins.assessment: One store/actor-owned flush capability feeds the common current-profile liveness ingress. Frame and CCall probes retain their distinct non-actor scopes; they do not drain another scope. Same-actor window probes reenter after the pending window has been taken. No duplicated producer-specific flush validators or parallel event authority was added.

The flush transaction commits before the separate durableOnly decision transaction. not_reached returns that durable successor; actor_process adopts it on both outcomes. This is the required source join, but the actual actor path has no new executed proof.

Existing probe checks are shared by durable admission and staged-window admission. Last qualifying capture is distinct from last capture/flush time; noise-only windows emit no activity probe. Result and stdout probes of one row share the existing underlying-observation clock identity. Existing scope, monotonic clock, interruption, terminal and source checks remain.

Existing transport owns one descriptor and writes captured bytes before classification. emitWindow fsyncs before its observer reference. Write/fsync failure is sticky and prevents a later callback from publishing that unavailable window. Drain precedes onProcessFinalized, descriptor close follows, and existing final archive comparison remains. These are static observations, not an executed failure proof.

Flush stays inside an existing transaction and returns a restore; rollback runs restores in reverse and commit discards them. Pending state is taken before recursive probe emission. New scopes tests exercise this through a declared stand-in; none has run on the final source.
